words.def: completely free of germs
words.ex: The nurse opened a sterile bandage for the cut.

words.def: to make something better by adding something good
words.ex: Compost will enrich the garden soil.

words.def: to dig carefully to uncover something buried
words.ex: Scientists excavate the desert to find dinosaur bones.

words.def: a season of strong winds and very heavy rain in some parts of the world
words.ex: Farmers wait for the monsoon to fill their rice fields with water.

words.def: from high up in the air
words.ex: The aerial photo showed every rooftop in our neighborhood.

words.def: something said to be funny, not to be taken seriously
words.ex: He said it in jest, so nobody was upset by the silly remark.

words.def: to lie in and enjoy warmth or light
words.ex: Lizards love to bask on warm rocks in the afternoon sun.

words.def: to lift something heavy, often with ropes
words.ex: The sailors hoist the flag up the pole.

words.def: to have or own something
words.ex: Do you possess a library card?

words.def: describing an angle that is smaller than a right angle
words.ex: Each corner of this triangle is an acute angle.

words.def: to show something for the first time by removing a cover
words.ex: The mayor will unveil the new statue on Friday.

words.def: one example of something, such as a plant or rock, used for study
words.ex: The scientist put a specimen of pond water under the microscope.

words.def: to become gradually thinner toward one end
words.ex: Carrots taper to a point at the bottom.

words.def: to give someone the tools or supplies needed for a job
words.ex: The club will equip each camper with a flashlight and a map.

words.def: to show that something is extra important
words.ex: The teacher underlined the date to emphasize it.

words.def: a narrow channel of water joining two larger bodies of water
words.ex: The ship sailed through the strait between the two seas.

words.def: a small mark or spot that spoils how something looks
words.ex: The apple was perfect except for one brown blemish on its skin.

words.def: an event in nature that can be seen and studied
words.ex: A rainbow is a beautiful phenomenon.

words.def: a sudden loss of power, success or happiness
words.ex: His pride and greed led to the downfall of the once-mighty king.

words.def: a substance that gives something its color
words.ex: The green pigment in leaves helps plants make food.

words.def: an odd-looking machine or gadget
words.ex: Grandpa built a strange contraption to feed the birds.

words.def: words carved or written on something, like a stone or coin
words.ex: The inscription on the old bell shows the year it was made.

words.def: a body part or behavior that helps a living thing survive where it lives
words.ex: Thick fur is an adaptation that keeps polar bears warm.

words.def: a tiny cell that a fern or mushroom releases to grow a new one
words.ex: A single spore landed on the wet log and began to grow.

words.def: in an area of homes at the edge of a city
words.ex: We live on a quiet suburban street near the city.

words.def: to poke with a finger or a stick
words.ex: Do not prod the sleeping dog.

words.def: the bottom number of a fraction, which tells how many equal parts make the whole
words.ex: In three fourths, the denominator is four.

words.def: bits of sand, mud, and rock that settle at the bottom of water
words.ex: Sediment piled up at the mouth of the river.

words.def: the size or amount of one part compared to the whole
words.ex: A large proportion of the class chose pizza for lunch.

words.def: to cut words or designs into a hard surface
words.ex: The jeweler will engrave my name on the back of the watch.

words.def: having a strong, pleasant smell
words.ex: The kitchen was full of aromatic spices for the holiday dinner.

words.def: the study of the parts of a body and how they fit together
words.ex: In anatomy class we learned where the lungs are.

words.def: so useful that its worth cannot be measured
words.ex: Your help with the bake sale was invaluable.

words.def: a feeling of being very tired
words.ex: After the long hike, fatigue made my legs heavy.

words.def: a small accident or piece of bad luck
words.ex: Except for one mishap with a spilled drink, the party went well.

words.def: to be very good at something, better than most
words.ex: Grace practices every day and hopes to excel at piano.

words.def: a book or paper written by hand or before it is printed
words.ex: The author mailed her manuscript to a publisher.

words.def: to wave or nod to someone to come closer
words.ex: The guide will beckon us to follow him.

words.def: a group of elected people who make the laws for a state or country
words.ex: The legislature voted on a new law about school buses.

words.def: protected from catching a disease
words.ex: After having chicken pox, most people are immune to it.

words.def: to give someone a job or object to take care of because you believe in them
words.ex: The family will entrust their dog to a neighbor while they travel.

words.def: not wasting money or materials
words.ex: Buying the big box of cereal is more economical.

words.def: clean in a way that keeps germs from spreading
words.ex: Washing your hands before you eat is a hygienic habit.

words.def: saying what you think openly and boldly
words.ex: Lila is outspoken about keeping the park clean.

words.def: a group of vehicles or ships traveling together for safety
words.ex: A convoy of trucks brought food to the flooded town.

words.def: to control something so it works the right way
words.ex: A thermostat helps regulate the temperature in the house.

words.def: a large pipe or channel built to carry water a long way
words.ex: Long ago, an aqueduct brought water to the city from the hills.

words.def: always working hard and keeping busy
words.ex: The industrious ants carried crumbs back to their hill all day.

words.def: an imaginary line through the center of an object that it spins around
words.ex: The earth spins on its axis once a day.

words.def: bold in a careless and silly way
words.ex: It was foolhardy to walk on the thin ice without checking it first.

words.def: a very hard, speckled rock often used for buildings
words.ex: The kitchen counter is made of gray granite.

words.def: to leave your home country to live in another one
words.ex: Her grandparents decided to emigrate across the ocean.

words.def: the top number of a fraction, which tells how many parts you have
words.ex: In two thirds, the numerator is two.

words.def: an animal that has a backbone
words.ex: A snake is a vertebrate because it has a backbone.

words.def: the distance around the edge of a circle
words.ex: We used string to measure the circumference of the tree trunk.

words.def: having to do with the national government of a country
words.ex: The federal government prints the country's money.

words.def: the answer you get when you divide one number by another
words.ex: When you divide twelve by three, the quotient is four.

words.def: busy, noisy activity with people moving around
words.ex: I love the bustle of the market on Saturday.

words.def: a tool that measures air pressure to help forecast weather
words.ex: The barometer dropped, so we knew a storm was coming.

words.def: ordinary writing in sentences and paragraphs, not poetry
words.ex: The book was written in prose, but each chapter ended with a poem.

words.def: able to speak two languages well
words.ex: My cousin is bilingual and speaks Spanish and English.

words.def: a cold, flat land with no trees where the ground stays frozen below the surface
words.ex: Caribou roam across the tundra in summer.

words.def: arranged in the order that events happened
words.ex: The timeline shows the events in chronological order.

words.def: nervous and mixed up because of being rushed or embarrassed
words.ex: He got flustered when he dropped his notes in front of the class.

words.def: a person who lives in a new settlement ruled by a faraway country
words.ex: Each colonist had to plant crops to have food for winter.

words.def: an animal that has no backbone
words.ex: A worm is an invertebrate.

words.def: land that is soaked with water, such as a marsh or swamp
words.ex: Herons hunt for fish in the wetland.

words.def: letting some light through but not clear enough to see through
words.ex: The translucent curtains let soft light into the room.

words.def: to carry or drag something heavy with effort
words.ex: We had to lug the heavy suitcase up the stairs.

words.def: a tube that carries blood away from the heart
words.ex: The doctor felt the pulse in the artery in my wrist.

words.def: describing an angle that is larger than a right angle but smaller than a straight line
words.ex: The open book made an obtuse angle.

words.def: to make a liquid weaker or thinner by adding water
words.ex: Dilute the juice with water so it is not so sweet.

words.def: a four-sided shape whose opposite sides are the same length and never meet
words.ex: A rectangle is a special kind of parallelogram.

words.def: a material that slows down the flow of heat or electricity
words.ex: Rubber is a good insulator, so it covers wires.

words.def: a short section at the beginning of a book or play that introduces it
words.ex: The prologue tells about the hero's life before the adventure.

words.def: able to break down naturally in soil without harming it
words.ex: These forks are biodegradable, so they won't pile up as trash.

words.def: a short section at the end of a book that tells what happened afterward
words.ex: In the epilogue, we learn the friends are still together years later.

words.def: a group of lines in a poem, like a paragraph in a story
words.ex: Each stanza of the poem has four lines.

words.def: a germ or other tiny creature, often one that spreads sickness or breaks things down
words.ex: A microbe can live in a single drop of water.

words.def: a comparison of two different things using like or as
words.ex: "Fast as a cheetah" is a simile.

words.def: to let fresh air into a room or space
words.ex: Open the windows to ventilate the kitchen.

words.def: using words in an imaginative way, not with their exact meaning
words.ex: "It's raining cats and dogs" is a figurative way of saying it is raining hard.

words.def: a four-sided shape with exactly one pair of parallel sides
words.ex: The bucket's side view looked like a trapezoid.

words.def: a living thing too small to see without a microscope
words.ex: A microorganism in the pond water swam across the glass slide.

words.def: a conclusion you reach by using clues and what you already know
words.ex: From the wet coats, I made the inference that it was raining.

words.def: describing rock formed when hot melted rock cools and hardens
words.ex: Obsidian is an igneous rock that looks like black glass.

words.def: a person who makes maps
words.ex: The cartographer drew every road and river on the new map.

words.def: the way heat moves through liquids and gases as warm parts rise and cool parts sink
words.ex: Convection carries warm air up toward the ceiling.

words.def: describing rock that was changed by great heat and pressure underground
words.ex: Marble is a metamorphic rock.

words.def: a stream or river that flows into a larger river
words.ex: A small tributary joins the river below the bridge.

words.def: giving human actions or feelings to things that are not human
words.ex: "The wind whispered" is an example of personification.

words.def: to begin to grow from a seed
words.ex: Bean seeds germinate in a few days.

words.def: a saying whose meaning is different from the meaning of its words
words.ex: "Break a leg" is an idiom that means good luck.

words.def: a point where two or more lines or edges meet, like the corner of a shape
words.ex: A triangle has a vertex at each of its three corners.

words.def: to give a hint about what will happen later in a story
words.ex: Dark clouds in chapter one foreshadow trouble ahead.

words.def: making electricity from the power of moving water
words.ex: The hydroelectric dam lights up the whole valley.

words.def: exactly the same shape and size
words.ex: The two halves of the square are congruent.

words.def: a large region of Earth with its own climate, plants, and animals, such as a desert or grassland
words.ex: The desert biome gets very little rain.

words.def: a flat, closed shape with three or more straight sides
words.ex: A triangle is the polygon with the fewest sides.

words.def: any flat shape with four straight sides
words.ex: A square is a quadrilateral.

words.def: a word that means the opposite of another word
words.ex: Cold is an antonym of hot.

words.def: an animal that eats both plants and meat
words.ex: A bear is an omnivore that eats berries and fish.

words.def: a word that sounds like the noise it names, like buzz or pop
words.ex: "Sizzle" is my favorite onomatopoeia.
